sections.heading: Tokens & Embeddings
sections.content: Text is split into tokens. Tokens are mapped to vectors (embeddings) that capture semantic relationships.

sections.heading: Transformer at a Glance
sections.caption: Tokens → Embeddings → Attention → Next‑token prediction, all dentro de una *context window*.

sections.heading: Attention
sections.content: Transformers use attention to weigh relevant tokens when predicting the next token. Multi‑head attention learns different relationships.

sections.heading: Inference & Context Window
sections.content: The model predicts one token at a time conditioned on prior tokens (prompt + generated). The maximum sequence length is the context window.

sections.heading: Cosine Similarity (pseudocode)
sections.content:
import numpy as np

# two embedding vectors
a = np.array([0.1, 0.3, -0.2])
b = np.array([0.05, 0.32, -0.18])

cos = np.dot(a, b) / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b))
print('similarity:', float(cos))

sections.heading: Mini‑Exercise: Embedding Similarity
sections.description: Compute and comparar similitud de embeddings de frases cortas.
steps: Obtén embeddings de: “The cat sat on the mat” y “A dog rested on the rug”.
Calcula el coseno: debería ser alto por similitud semántica.
Prueba con una frase no relacionada (e.g., “The stock market rose today”) y observa cómo cae la similitud.
Opcional: crea un pequeño índice y recupera los 3 vecinos más cercanos por similitud.
